lessons.title: Diminutives: -tjie, -ie, -jie
explanation: Afrikaans speakers love making words "little": for size, cuteness, or friendliness. The ending depends on how the word ends:

| ending of the word | add | examples |
|---|---|---|
| -d, -t | **-jie** | hond → **hondjie**, kat → **katjie** |
| -m | **-pie** | boom → **boompie**, arm → **armpie** |
| -k, -g, -p, -f, -s | **-ie** | boek → **boekie**, dag → **daggie**, kop → **koppie** |
| a vowel, or -l, -n, -r, -w | **-tjie** | tafel → **tafeltjie**, deur → **deurtjie**, vrou → **vroutjie** |
| short vowel + -l, -m, -n, -r | double + **-etjie** | man → **mannetjie**, bal → **balletjie** |
After a short vowel the consonant often doubles: kop → **koppie**, vis → **vissie**.
Plurals of diminutives just add **-s**: hondjie → **hondjies**.

examples.af: Die kinders speel met die katjies.
examples.en: The children are playing with the kittens.

exercises.en: A small dog is a little dog.
A small tree is a little tree.
A small table is a little table.
A small head is a little head (also: a cup).
A small man is a little man.

lessons.title: Adjectives before nouns
explanation: When an adjective comes **after** the noun ("the man is friendly"), it never changes: **Die man is vriendelik.**
When it comes **before** the noun, longer adjectives usually add **-e**: **'n vriendelike man**, **'n lelike hond**, **'n gelukkige kind**.
Short, common adjectives often stay the same: **'n groot huis**, **'n mooi meisie**, **'n klein kind**, **'n rooi kar**.
Some change shape before a noun: **oud → ou** (die ou man), **nuut → nuwe** (die nuwe kar), **goed → goeie** (goeie môre!), **jonk → jong**, **lank → lang**.
Comparing: **groot → groter → grootste**, **mooi → mooier → mooiste**, and the irregular **goed → beter → beste**.

examples.af: Die ou man is baie vriendelik.
examples.en: The old man is very friendly.

examples.af: My broer is groter as ek.
examples.en: My brother is bigger than me.

exercises.en: The old man is my grandpa.
My brother is bigger than me.
